groups.title: Testing Philosophy
groups.question: You need to test your Next.js app before every release: validation logic, components and the sign-in and checkout flows. Explain your testing approach.

followUps.Unit testing server and client logic wit: What would you unit test with Vitest?
followUps.Component testing with React Testing Lib: How does React Testing Library encourage good component tests?
followUps.End-to-end testing strategy with Playwri: Which flows would you cover with Playwright and why only a few?

evidence.text: Vitest is a fast test runner compatible with Jest's API.
Pure functions, Zod schemas and server action logic are good unit test targets.
These tests catch regressions quickly on every change.
It renders components and finds elements by role and label.
Tests focus on what users see and do, not internals.
Such tests survive refactors that do not change behaviour.
Playwright drives real browsers through full flows.
It covers critical paths like sign-in, checkout and form submission.
These tests are slower, so they are kept to the most important flows.

notEnough: Only saying you write E2E tests.

groups.title: Deployment Architecture
groups.question: You are deploying to Vercel with a PostgreSQL database, and after launch you see 'too many connections' errors. Explain the deployment setup and the cause.

followUps.Vercel project structure and environment: How do Vercel projects and environments work?
followUps.Production database setup with connectio: Why do serverless functions exhaust database connections, and what fixes it?

evidence.text: Connecting the repository deploys on every push.
Production, preview and development have separate environment variables.
Each branch or pull request can get its own deployment.
Many serverless instances each open their own connections.
PostgreSQL has a limited number of connections, which runs out under load.
A connection pooler like PgBouncer or Prisma Accelerate shares a small pool of connections.

groups.title: Testing Tooling
groups.question: You are writing your first Playwright tests, isolating unit tests from Prisma and running everything on pull requests. Explain how you would set this up.

followUps.Writing and running Playwright E2E tests: How do you write and generate Playwright tests?
followUps.Mocking modules and fetch calls in Vites: How does vi.mock isolate code from Prisma or fetch?
followUps.Continuous integration with GitHub Actio: What should a GitHub Actions workflow run on pull requests?

evidence.text: Tests use page actions like goto and click with expectations on the page.
The codegen tool records actions in a browser and writes test code.
Playwright waits automatically, avoiding fixed sleeps.
vi.mock replaces a module with a controlled fake.
Tests decide what the fake returns.
Tests run without a real database or network and give the same result every time.
It runs unit tests and Playwright tests on every pull request.
Failing checks block merging broken code.
Caching dependencies keeps the pipeline fast.

groups.title: Vercel Deployment
groups.question: Reviewers want to see UI changes before merge, and after launch you want to know how fast the site is for real users. Explain preview deployments and Vercel's monitoring.

followUps.Preview deployments for pull request rev: What does a preview deployment give reviewers?
followUps.Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights moni: What do Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights report?

evidence.text: Each pull request gets its own deployment URL.
Reviewers test the change on production-like infrastructure.
Problems are found before the change reaches production.
Analytics tracks real user page views.
Speed Insights reports Core Web Vitals like LCP and CLS from real users.
Both are enabled by installing a package and adding a component.

notEnough: Only saying they monitor the site.
